classification.difficultyReason: Select substitution, radical isolation or denominator clearing to suit each equation. The hardest case requires squaring twice, solving the resulting quadratic and rejecting an extraneous root; the instruction explicitly prompts solution checking.

content.prompt: Solve these equations for $x$. (Make sure you check your solutions.)

answer.worked:
The domain is $x\geq0$. Let $t=\sqrt{x}$, so $t\geq0$ and $x=t^2$.

$$\begin{align*}6t^2-t&=12\\6t^2-t-12&=0\\(3t+4)(2t-3)&=0\end{align*}$$

Thus $t=-\frac43$ or $t=\frac32$. Reject the negative value because $t=\sqrt{x}\geq0$.

$$x=\left(\frac32\right)^2=\frac94.$$

Check:

$$\begin{align*}6\left(\frac94\right)-\sqrt{\frac94}&=\frac{27}{2}-\frac32\\6\left(\frac94\right)-\sqrt{\frac94}&=12\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$x=2$

Isolate a radical, square twice and check the candidates.
answer.worked:
The domain is $\frac57\leq x\leq\frac{15}{7}$.

$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{7x-5}&=\sqrt{2x}+\sqrt{15-7x}\\7x-5&=15-5x+2\sqrt{2x(15-7x)}\\6x-10&=\sqrt{30x-14x^2}\end{align*}$$

The last equation requires $x\geq\frac53$. Squaring again gives:

$$\begin{align*}(6x-10)^2&=30x-14x^2\\36x^2-120x+100&=30x-14x^2\\50x^2-150x+100&=0\\x^2-3x+2&=0\\(x-1)(x-2)&=0\end{align*}$$

The candidates are $x=1$ and $x=2$. Reject $x=1$, which violates $x\geq\frac53$; in the original equation its left side is $0$ and its right side is $\sqrt8$.

Check $x=2$:

$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{7(2)-5}-\sqrt{2(2)}&=3-2=1\\\sqrt{15-7(2)}&=1\end{align*}$$

Therefore $x=2$.

The denominators require $x>0$. Let $t=\sqrt{x}$, so $t>0$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{6t-11}{3t}&=\frac{2t+1}{t+6}\\(6t-11)(t+6)&=3t(2t+1)\\6t^2+25t-66&=6t^2+3t\\22t&=66\\t&=3\\x&=9\end{align*}$$

Check:

$$\begin{align*}\frac{6\sqrt9-11}{3\sqrt9}&=\frac79\\\frac{2\sqrt9+1}{\sqrt9+6}&=\frac79\end{align*}$$

Both denominators are nonzero.

answer.short:
$x=8$

Multiply by $\sqrt{9+2x}$ before isolating and squaring the remaining radical.
answer.worked:
The domain is $x\geq0$, so $\sqrt{9+2x}>0$. Multiply by $\sqrt{9+2x}$:

$$\begin{align*}9+2x-\sqrt{2x(9+2x)}&=5\\\sqrt{18x+4x^2}&=4+2x\\18x+4x^2&=(4+2x)^2\\18x+4x^2&=16+16x+4x^2\\2x&=16\\x&=8\end{align*}$$

Check:

$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{9+2(8)}-\sqrt{2(8)}&=5-4=1\\\frac5{\sqrt{9+2(8)}}&=1\end{align*}$$
